citation.title: Explainable quantum neural networks for multi-material topology optimization
citation.authors: Dahyun Joo, Naruethep Sukulthanasorn, Kenjiro Terada, Do-Nyun Kim

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: The ten-qubit model predicts multi-material layouts from intermediate MMA fields, with reported material-label accuracy of 81.4–94.0% and transfer to unseen conditions and meshes.
claim.alternatives: The abstract emphasizes interpretability and generalization to out-of-distribution boundary conditions and three-dimensional layouts; Results §2.3 also discusses the early-stop time–accuracy trade-off.

baseline.implementation: MMA-based MMTO solver adapted from MATLAB code (Methods §4.1)
baseline.hardware_ml: AMD Ryzen 7 9700X 8-Core Processor for exact statevector evaluation (Methods §4.3); MMA hardware not stated
baseline.problem_size: Training/validation and OOD: 50×25 mesh; high-resolution and 3D transfer cases also evaluated (Results §2.2–2.4, Table S1)
baseline.classical_iterations: Terminal grayscale ratio below 0.02 for regular 2D/3D and below 0.01 for high-resolution cases (Methods §4.1)
baseline.quality_metric: Material-type pixel accuracy and normalized compliance Cpred/CGT (Results §§2.2–2.4)
baseline.quality_gap: Validation accuracy 81.4–94.0%; OOD, high-resolution and 3D accuracy/compliance also reported (Results §§2.2–2.4).

R1.evidence: Abstract and Results §2: primary outcome is prediction quality relative to terminal MMA layouts; no primary speed comparison.

R2.evidence: Methods §4.1–4.3: no R2 inefficiency criterion for the baseline can be established from the reported text.

R3.evidence: Abstract and Methods §4.3: paper gives no quantitative speed claim or training/data cost accounting.

R4.evidence: Results §§2.3–2.4: returned predictions are compared using material accuracy and normalized compliance, but infeasible/failure rates are not reported.

reporting.n_test_cases: Training T1–T3, validation V1–V3, OOD O1–O4, high-resolution HR1–HR3, and 3D1–3D4 (Results §2).

notes: Code and data are stated as available on request (Methods §§5–6); public runnable code was not located.
